charts.title: Most popular sports participated in South Korea in 2022
charts.short: Most popular sports participated South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey about the most popular sports in South Korea in 2022, around 49 percent of respondents stated that they took walks as their favorite sport, while another 23.5 percent chose hiking. Aside from these top two favorite sports, indoor sports activities such as bowling or gymnastics were popular. That year, about 61 percent of the respondents were taking part in regular sports activities at least once a week.
charts.note: South Korea; September 6 to November 12, 2022; 9,000 respondents; 10 years and older

charts.title: Average monthly spending on doing sports in South Korea in 2022 (in 1,000 South Korean won)
charts.short: Monthly spending on doing sports South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey about sports participation in South Korea in 2022, around 24 percent of the respondents stated that they paid no money to play sports or exercise. About 19 percent of the respondents said they spent between 30 thousand and 60 thousand South Korean won per month for sports and working out. The average monthly expenses in 2022 was around 77,135 won. That year, about 61 percent of the respondents were taking part in regular sports activities at least once a week.
charts.note: South Korea; September 6 to November 12, 2022; 9,000 respondents; 10 years and older; those that regularly participate in sports

charts.title: Interest in taking care of health in South Korea as of July 2022
charts.short: Interest in taking care of health South Korea 2022
charts.description: In July 2022, according to a survey conducted in South Korea by Opensurvey, around 68.8 percent of respondents said that they were interested in taking care of their health. Less than four percent of all respondents stated to be uninterested in taking care of their health.
charts.note: South Korea; July 23, 2022; 1,000 respondents; 20-69 years

charts.title: Reasons why people participate in sports activities in South Korea in 2022
charts.short: Reasons why people are doing sports South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey about sports participation in South Korea in 2022, around 77 percent of the respondents stated that they played sports or exercised to maintain their health. About another 48 percent said they worked out to control their weight. That year, about 61 percent of the respondents were taking part in regular sports activities at least once a week.
charts.note: South Korea; September 6 to November 12, 2022; 9,000 respondents; 10 years and older; those that regularly participate in sports

charts.title: Number of fitness centers registered in South Korea from 2010 to 2021
charts.short: Fitness centers number South Korea 2010-2021
charts.description: There were around 11.1 thousand fitness centers registered in South Korea in 2021. This was an increase from the previous year and the highest recorded number during the surveyed period. The number has increased continuously over the past years from a little over six thousand fitness centers in 2010.
charts.note: South Korea; 2010 to 2021

charts.title: Number of fitness centers registered in South Korea in 2021, by region
charts.short: Number of fitness centers South Korea 2021, by region
charts.description: In 2021, there were more than 2.9 thousand fitness studios registered in Seoul, South Korea. The province of Gyeonggi ranked second with around 2.6 thousand gyms. That year, there were over 11.1 thousand fitness studios in the country.
charts.note: South Korea; 2021

charts.title: Number of newly licensed grade 2 bodybuilding instructors in South Korea from 2014 to 2022 (in 1,000s)
charts.short: Number of licensed grade 2 bodybuilding instructors South Korea 2014-2022
charts.description: In 2022, there were around 7.5 thousand newly certified grade 2 instructors for bodybuilding in South Korea. This was a decrease from the previous year, with a sharp decrease recorded in 2020. Anyone over the age of 18 is eligible to apply for a grade 2 leisure sports instructor certification, which entails a written and practical exam. Licensed bodybuilding instructors are able to work as personal trainers at fitness studios.
charts.note: South Korea; 2014 to 2022

charts.title: Number of newly licensed youth bodybuilding instructors in South Korea from 2015 to 2022
charts.short: Number of licensed youth bodybuilding instructors South Korea 2015-2022
charts.description: In 2022, there were 406 newly certified youth sports instructors for bodybuilding in South Korea. This was a decrease from the previous year, which had the highest figure recorded with 530 new licensees. Anyone over the age of 18 is eligible to apply for youth sports instructor certification, which entails exams and additional training periods.
charts.note: South Korea; 2015 to 2022

charts.title: Number of newly licensed elderly bodybuilding instructors in South Korea from 2015 to 2022
charts.short: Number of licensed elderly bodybuilding instructors South Korea 2015-2022
charts.description: In 2022, there were 885 newly certified elderly bodybuilding instructors in South Korea. This was a decrease from the previous year, which had the highest figure recorded with over one thousand new licensees. Anyone over the age of 18 is eligible to apply for elderly sports instructor certification, which entails exams and additional training periods.
charts.note: South Korea; 2015 to 2022

charts.title: Day of the week to participate in sports activities in South Korea in 2022
charts.short: Day of the week doing sports South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey about sports participation in South Korea in 2022, around 39 percent of the respondents stated that they played sports or exercised on weekdays. Another 62.3 percent said they played on weekdays or the weekend. That year, about 61 percent of the respondents were taking part in regular sports activities at least once a week.
charts.note: South Korea; September 6 to November 12, 2022; 9,000 respondents; 10 years and older; those that regularly participate in sports

charts.title: Time of the day to participate in sports activities in South Korea in 2022
charts.short: Time of the day doing sports South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey about sports participation in South Korea in 2022, around 37 percent of the respondents stated that they played sports or exercised in the evenings between 6pm and 10pm. After evenings, mornings were the most popular times for working out. That year, about 61 percent of the respondents were taking part in regular sports activities at least once a week.
charts.note: South Korea; September 6 to November 12, 2022; 9,000 respondents; 10 years and older; those that regularly participate in sports

charts.title: Intensity of exercise for South Koreans as of July 2022
charts.short: Intensity of exercise South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey conducted in South Korea by Opensurvey in July 2022, over 60 percent of surveyed respondents answered that they exercised with moderate intensity. Around 11.5 percent stated to engage in high intensity exercise, while another roughly 28.4 percent said they participated in low intensity exercise.
charts.note: South Korea; July 23, 2022; 845 respondents; 20-69 years; those that currently participate in sports

charts.title: Duration of exercise in South Korea as of July 2022
charts.short: Exercise duration South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Opensurvey in July 2022 in South Korea, more than 42 percent of respondents stated to exercise between 30 minutes to an hour. The average duration of exercise among respondents was a little over one hour.
charts.note: South Korea; July 23, 2022; 845 respondents; 20-69 years; those that currently participate in sports

charts.title: Fitness and health service purchases in South Korea as of March 2024
charts.short: Fitness and health service purchases in South Korea 2024
charts.description: 10 percent of South Korean respondents answer our survey on "Fitness and health service purchases" with "Gym membership". The survey was conducted in 2024, among 2,020 consumers.
charts.note: South Korea; April 2023 to March 2024; 2020 respondents; 18-64 years
charts.source: Statista Consumer Insights Share of respondents

charts.short: Fitness and health service online purchases in South Korea 2024
charts.description: 5 percent of South Korean respondents answer our survey on "Fitness and health service online purchases" with "Fitness, yoga, and training". The survey was conducted in 2024, among 2,020 consumers.

charts.title: Share of South Koreans who used scientific fitness management services from 2017 to 2022
charts.short: Usage of scientific fitness management services South Korea 2017-2022
charts.description: According to a survey about sports participation in South Korea in 2022, around 13 percent of the respondents stated that they were making use of scientific fitness management services. That year, about 61 percent of the respondents were taking part in regular sports activities at least once a week.
charts.note: South Korea; September 6 to November 12, 2022; 9,000 respondents; 10 years and older

charts.title: Leading fitness apps in South Korea as of April 2023, by user coverage
charts.short: Leading fitness apps South Korea 2023, by user coverage
charts.description: In April 2023, Samsung Health recorded a user coverage share of almost 53 percent, meaning that over half of all fitness app users used this app. Another leading app was CashWalk, which provides users the opportunity to receive rewards by walking.
charts.note: South Korea; April 2023; including Android OS and iOS

charts.title: Most popular fitness YouTube channels in South Korea as of August 2023, by number of followers (in millions)
charts.short: Popular fitness channels on YouTube South Korea 2023, by number of subscribers
charts.description: As of August 2023, the fitness channel Physical Gallery had the most subscribers on the online video sharing platform YouTube in South Korea, with approximately 3.1 million subscribers. Following this channel, Thankyou BUBU had the second highest number of subscribers, with about 3.03 million.
charts.note: South Korea; August 2023
charts.source: NoxInfluencer Number of followers in millions

charts.title: Fitness and health logging in South Korea as of July 2022
charts.short: Fitness and health logging South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Opensurvey in July 2022 in South Korea, around 30 percent of respondents kept a record of their activity and exercise such as step counts or pictures. The majority did not do such logging, with nearly 56 percent answering to not keep any records of their fitness and health.
charts.note: South Korea; July 23, 2022; 1,000 respondents; 20-69 years
categories: Activity and exercise records (step count, workout routine, pictures, etc.)
Physical records (weight, blood pressure, heart rate, etc.)
Everyday habit records (diet, nutrients, calories, etc.)
Do not separately record such things

charts.title: Fitness and health logging methods in South Korea as of July 2022
charts.short: Fitness and health logging methods South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Opensurvey in July 2022 in South Korea, around 67 percent of respondents logged their fitness and health automatically via a smartphone application or device. About 22 percent kept a manual record of their health status.
charts.note: South Korea; July 23, 2022; 443 respondents; 20-69 years; those that log their fitness and health
categories: Automatic recording via app or device

charts.title: Devices used for fitness and health logging in South Korea as of July 2022
charts.short: Devices used for fitness and health logging South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Opensurvey in July 2022 in South Korea, around 39 percent of respondents used a fitness device that could be synced with their smartphoen to log their fitness and health. Nearly 31 percent answered to use a smartwatch, while about 17 percent kept a manual record of their activity.
charts.note: South Korea; July 23, 2022; 443 respondents; 20-69 years; those that log their fitness and health

charts.title: Reasons for sharing fitness and health logs in South Korea as of July 2022
charts.short: Reasons for sharing fitness and health logs South Korea 2022
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Opensurvey in July 2022 in South Korea, around 37.5 percent of respondents shared their logs of fitness and health activities to keep a record of it. For about 26 percent of respondents, motivation or entertainment was a factor, while roughly 34.5 percent did not share their records about their fitness.
charts.note: South Korea; July 23, 2022; 443 respondents; 20-69 years; those that log their fitness and health
categories: Have never shared records of fitness and health

charts.title: Ownership rate of wearable devices in South Korea from 2016 to 2022
charts.short: Wearable device ownership South Korea 2016-2022
charts.description: According to a survey on wearable devices in South Korea, about 11.6 percent of the respondents aged 6 years and older owned wearable devices in 2022, compared to only around 1.9 percent in 2016. The ownership rate of wearable devices has steadily increased in recent years.
charts.note: South Korea; 2016 to 2022; 25,000 households; 6 years and older
charts.source: Korean Internet & Security Agency; Market Metrix; Ministry of Science and ICT (South Korea); NIA

charts.title: Ownership of smartwatches and wearable fitness/activity trackers in South Korea as of September 2022
charts.short: Smartwatch and wearable fitness/activity trackers ownership South Korea 2022
charts.description: A survey conducted by Rakuten Insight in September 2022 in South Korea found that around 36.75 percent of respondents owned a smartwatch, while another 3.17 percent stated that they owned both a smartwatch and a fitness/activity tracker.
charts.note: South Korea; September 8 to 30, 2022; 7,466 respondents; 16 years and older
categories: Yes, both a smartwatch and a fitness/activity tracker

charts.title: Brands used by owners of smartwatch or wearable fitness/activity trackers in South Korea as of September 2022
charts.short: Smartwatch or wearable fitness/activity trackers brands owned South Korea 2022
charts.description: A survey conducted by Rakuten Insight in September 2022 in South Korea found that around 61.1 percent of respondents who owned a smartwatch or a fitness/activity tracker owned a wearable device by Samsung.
charts.note: South Korea; September 8 to 30, 2022; 3,389 respondents; 16 years and older; owners of smartwatches or wearable fitness/activity trackers

charts.title: Motivation for purchasing smartwatches or wearable fitness/activity trackers in South Korea as of September 2022
charts.short: Reasons for buying wearable tech South Korea 2022
charts.description: A survey conducted by Rakuten Insight in September 2022 found that the main motivation for purchasing a wearable device was to have easier accessibility to smartphone functions, with around 52.4 percent of surveyed wearable tech owners answering that way.
charts.note: South Korea; September 8 to 30, 2022; 3,389 respondents; 16 years and older; consumers that own smartwatches or wearable fitness/activity trackers
categories: I wanted easier accessibility to smartphone functions without having to constantly have my smartphone in my hand
I am concerned about my health and want to monitor and improve it (such as sleep quality, measuring heart rate, number of steps taken a day, etc)
I already own other smart devices from the same brand (such as smartphones, televisions, etc) and want to stay connected with my other devices easier
The price is reasonable for the functions that it can do
I am into fitness and want to keep track of and optimize my training and performance
I like to keep up with the latest tech trends and products

charts.title: Popular type of apps connected to smartwatches and fitness/activity trackers in South Korea as of September 2022
charts.short: Apps connected to smartwatches and fitness trackers South Korea 2022
charts.description: A survey conducted by Rakuten Insight in September 2022 found that most respondents claimed that they connected their wearable tech with fitness apps like Runtastic, Runkeeper, MapMyRun and similar.
charts.note: South Korea; September 8 to 30, 2022; 3,389 respondents; 16 years and older; consumers that own smartwatches and/or fitness/activity trackers
categories: Mobile payment apps (Apple Pay, Android Pay, Samsung Pay, Fitbit Pay, Garmin Pay, etc)
Smart home apps (Nest, Philips Hue, etc)
